observations.explanation: The paper describes the three-stage hierarchical localization process—files, code elements, then edit locations—on PDF pp. 3–4. “Reproducible-in-principle” is appropriately qualified; the paper also says it open-sourced AGENTLESS (p. 1).

Table 3 and its discussion report 70 fixes for a single greedy sample at $0.11 average cost, 78 after multiple samples and majority voting, and 82 after test filtering, at $0.34 (PDF p. 8). This supports the stated improvements and associated cost.

The paper says baseline results are taken from the official leaderboard or tools’ papers/repositories, and notes that many closed-source systems provide neither source code nor trajectories for verification (PDF pp. 6–7).

The implementation uses GPT-4o and the evaluation focuses on SWE-bench Lite (PDF p. 6). The paper reports no broader evaluation across models or benchmarks, so the stated limit on what the comparison establishes is justified.
